bandReport.notes: Complete: Q60-80, 21 questions, contiguous with no gap. Footers read (13-B), (15-B), (17-B), (19-B) — all Series B. Per-page: p13 Q60-65, p15 Q66-69, p17 Q70-75, p19 Q76-80. SEAMS BOTH CLEAN: the page before (p11, footer 11-B) ends with Q59 complete at the page foot, and the page after (p21, footer 21-B) opens at Q81, so no question is stranded at either edge and none is owned by nobody. NO NUMBERING JUMP: my pages are consecutive ODD printed pages (the even pages are the Hindi counterparts that Part B alternates with and which the render deliberately skips), and the numbering runs unbroken across every page turn (65->66, 69->70, 75->76), which is the evidence no English page was skipped in this band. NO DEVANAGARI PAGE: every page is printed English. p15 carries faint Devanagari SHOW-THROUGH from the Hindi reverse face (grey, mirrored, behind the text) — that is the paper, not a Hindi page; the printed English is sharp and black and the footer reads 15-B. The booklet sets decimals with a mid-dot (5.6 prints as 5*6, 0.20 as 0*20); written here as ordinary decimal points, matching the convention the Series D band files already use. Q77(d) is a radical over 10 only: sqrt(10) m/s. Q70's options (a) and (d) carry no trailing 'only' while (b) and (c) do — transcribed as printed, not normalised.

questions.stem: A bicycle racing track is a level circular road of radius 10 m. Three cyclists P, Q and R with identical cycles are cycling on the track with speeds 2 m/s, 3 m/s and 5 m/s respectively. If the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road is 0.1, then which cyclist will slip? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)

The bob of a simple pendulum is displaced from its mean position and then released from rest 0.20 m above its mean position. What is the speed of the bob as it passes through the mean position? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)

A tennis ball of mass 350 g is thrown vertically upwards at a speed of 4 m/s. If M is the maximum gravitational potential energy of the ball and H is the maximum height it reaches, then which one of the following is correct? (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
Which of the following is correct regarding the total internal reflection at the interface between two different optical media?

options.label: A
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index.

options.label: B
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

options.label: C
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing at any angle from a medium of high refractive index to a medium of low refractive index.

options.label: D
options.text: The phenomenon of total internal reflection can occur only if light is passing from a medium of low refractive index to a medium of high refractive index and at an angle greater than the critical angle.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements (I. the weight of an object is the same everywhere on the surface of the Earth, but its inertial mass could be different; II. the inertial mass and gravitational mass of an object are proportional and the proportionality constant is the same everywhere; III. the inertial mass and weight of an object are the same at different places on Earth) — which is/are correct?
